question: A 33-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of severe right flank pain for 2 hours. The pain is colicky in nature and she describes it as 9 out of 10 in intensity. She has had 2 episodes of vomiting. She has no history of similar episodes in the past. She is 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weighs 104 kg (229 lb); BMI is 41 kg/m2. Her temperature is 37.3°C (99.1°F), pulse is 96/min, respirations are 16/min and blood pressure is 116/76 mm Hg. The abdomen is soft and there is mild tenderness to palpation in the right lower quadrant. Bowel sounds are reduced. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Her leukocyte count is 7,400/mm3. A low-dose CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis shows a round 12-mm stone in the distal right ureter. Urine dipstick is mildly positive for blood. Microscopic examination of the urine shows RBCs and no WBCs. 0.9% saline infusion is begun and intravenous ketorolac is administered. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient presents with severe right flank pain" -> "CT scan shows 12-mm stone in distal right ureter" -> "Stone likely causing obstruction and pain" -> "Patient requires intervention for stone removal" -> "Ureterorenoscopy is a direct method to remove ureteral stones" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has colicky flank pain and vomiting" -> "CT scan reveals a 12-mm stone in distal right ureter" -> "Stone may lead to complications if not addressed" -> "Ureteral stenting can relieve obstruction and manage pain" -> "Stenting is less invasive than ureteroscopy" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient has a 12-mm stone in distal right ureter" -> "Observation may lead to worsening symptoms or complications" -> "Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy is less effective for larger stones" -> "Ureterorenoscopy is preferred for stones of this size" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has mild hematuria and flank pain" -> "CT scan confirms ureteral stone" -> "Immediate intervention is necessary to prevent complications" -> "Ureterorenoscopy is the most definitive treatment" -> 90%
analysis: The patient has a 12-mm stone in the distal right ureter, which is causing severe flank pain and associated symptoms. Given the size of the stone and the patient's symptoms, ureterorenoscopy (option a) is the most appropriate next step in management. This procedure allows for direct visualization and removal of the stone, which is indicated for stones larger than 5 mm that cause significant symptoms. Other options like observation or ureteral stenting may not adequately address the immediate issue of the obstructing stone.
